subject: Re: MSA and Order Form — SLA / support redlines
messages:
From: Priya Shah <pshah@optimacloud.io>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@optimacloud.io
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — SLA clarifications and proposed parity on credits

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the draft — we ran the SLA sections past Procurement and Legal and have a few open items we'd like to resolve before we proceed to signature. High-level asks below, details are in the attached Optima_SLA_questionnaire.xlsx:

- Uptime measurement: we need the metric and sampling window defined (are you measuring per-region availability or global?). Please confirm which endpoints and what counts as "traffic" for the calculation.
- Service credits: the tiering looks aggressive on the credit amounts (60% cap for a P1 is concerning). Can we shift to a monthly credit cap (e.g., 2x monthly fees) and a rolling 12-month aggregate cap?
- Response times: P1 response window is stated as 1 hour — request to change to "1 hour to acknowledge, 4 hours to provide initial remediation plan" to match our incident cadence.
- Maintenance windows: Optima prefers staggered maintenance lanes (region A/B/C) and a maximum single maintenance blackout of 4 hours. We need a guaranteed 30-day notice for scheduled windows >2 hours and a commitment to avoid overlap on regional lanes.

We'd also like to see a clause for fallback model/region routing (commercial fallback) so that we can route to a secondary region without triggering a credit if Redwood initiates the failover.

We're hoping to close commercial redlines this week — can your team confirm changes and share a marked-up Order Form / SLA?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Procurement, OptimaCloud
procurement@optimacloud.io

Attachment: Optima_SLA_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet with detailed asks)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@optimacloud.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — SLA clarifications and proposed parity on credits

Priya — thanks for the precise notes and the questionnaire. Attaching our initial redline (Redwood_SLA_Redline_v1.docx) that addresses each bullet; summary highlights below.

Summary of our proposed changes (high level):
- Uptime measurement: we propose a per-region rolling 30-day measurement using success-rate over sampled 1-minute buckets for the customer-facing REST generation endpoints. We'll add explicit endpoint URIs and sampling cadence in the Order Form appendix.
- Service credits: agree to add a monthly cap rather than a raw percentage cap. Proposed language: monthly credits capped at 2x the monthly invoice for the impacted subscription, 12-month rolling cap at 6x. We kept the step function for thresholds but softened the % for the mid-tier.
- Response times: accept the split you suggested for P1s: 1 hour acknowledgement and 4 hours for initial remediation plan. We'll preserve faster SLAs for Dedicated customers.
- Maintenance windows and lanes: we propose a "staggered lane" approach — three lanes per region (A/B/C), no overlapping scheduled maintenance in the same lane across regions for critical services, and 30-day notice for >2 hour windows. For emergency maintenance we'll commit to best-effort notice and a post-event report.
- Fallback routing: will include a commercial fallback exception where Redwood-initiated cross-region failover does not trigger credits provided we meet defined RTO and notify within the SLA window.

Next steps: 1) Jonas (Legal) — please review the redline and flag any broad MSA language (caps, force majeure, measurement definitions) that need legal rewording; 2) Karthik — I'll need a commercial concession option if Legal pushes back on the monthly cap; 3) Priya — once we have legal wording we can circulate a clean Order Form for signature.

I've attached the doc. If this looks good we'll aim to get Legal comments back by EOD Friday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0186

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Redline_v1.docx (marked-up Order Form + appendix)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — legal redlines (SLA appendix)

Laura/Karthik — read through Laura's redline. A few legal items we should include in the MSA/Order Form redline before sending back to Optima:

1) Measurement definitions: tighten the language around the sampling window and the list of endpoints included; avoid language that allows endpoint inclusion to be expanded post-signature. I'll add an appendix table enumerating URIs and sampling cadence.

2) Credit caps: acceptable to move to a monthly cap, but we should add a hard annual cap and a carveout for customer-initiated downtime (e.g., changes triggered by Optima). Proposed legal wording: "Monthly credits will not exceed the lesser of 2x the monthly subscription fee or $250,000; aggregate credits in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed 6x the applicable monthly subscription fee."

3) Force majeure and Third-party outage: add a narrow exception for outages caused by third-party cloud providers or force majeure events; require Redwood to provide reasonable evidence.

4) Maintenance notice: 30-day notice for scheduled maintenance >2 hours is fine; recommend including a right to reschedule by Optima once per year without penalty if it materially impacts their blackout calendar.

5) Indemnity / liability caps: ensure we are not creating broad unlimited liability through SLO language — add explicit cross-reference to MSA liability caps.

I'll produce a PDF with marked sections and proposed MSA language for review (attached). If we accept the monthly caps commercially, ask Sales to check for any carveouts they need for strategic customers.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_legal_comments.pdf (legal comments and proposed wording)

Hi Priya — looping in a quick commercial option to help close: if Optima signs the Order Form within 30 days, Redwood can offer one month of Dedicated capacity at no charge (applies to the first month only) and commit to a joint runbook review within 30 days of go-live. That concession helps us meet the monthly credit cap expectations while keeping long-term liability bounded.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 06/22: Legal and Ops finalize a clean redline and circulate to Optima (Jonas + Laura)
- Wed 06/23: Commercial concession incorporated into Order Form
- Thu 06/24: Optima signoff window opens (DocuSign link below)

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/LAURA/OPTI-1842
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/OPTI-1842

Priya — please let me know if this commercial package is sufficient; happy to jump on a 20-minute call to close remaining points.

Thanks,
